Forward-Deployed Engineering

Inside the customer's systems.
Accountable through to production.

On these engagements I worked inside the customer's own environment, against live systems and real data, and stayed with the work until it ran in production. This page summarizes how that went and points to the written case study behind every claim.

40+ accounts AWS accounts under one governance model
$300K+ Annual infrastructure savings identified
≥ 25% Projected compute savings, Tanzu to EKS assessment
~93% Lighter first load on a product I built and run

How I worked

Three habits across every engagement

What stayed constant whether the work was a landing zone, a database migration, or an assessment.

01 · Direct presence

Worked with the operators

I worked alongside the people who ran the systems, which surfaced the legacy behavior, data quirks, and compliance constraints that requirements documents leave out.

02 · Live systems

Built against real environments

The designs and code were written and tested against the real systems and security rules: database synchronization, failover orchestration, and infrastructure code.

03 · Production ownership

Left evidence behind

Each engagement ended with something the customer's team could run and check: tested infrastructure code, runbooks, and recorded design decisions.

Customer engagements

Work done under real production constraints

Sectors where downtime carries a high financial or public cost. Customer names are withheld; the case studies describe each design and its trade-offs.

Electronic tolling infrastructure

Designed one governed AWS foundation under 40+ accounts, with a hub-and-spoke Transit Gateway network and Aurora disaster-recovery environments kept in parity with the primary.

See the tolling case studies

Telecom platform

Moved a legacy database tier to Aurora with continuous replication and connection pooling, and automated failover while preserving a node-locked software license.

See the telecom case studies

Regulated healthcare platform

Decomposed an on-premise clinical monolith, integrated medical devices over HL7, and shipped through a gated pipeline. The cost work identified $300K+ in annual infrastructure savings across engagements.

See the healthcare case studies

AWS migration assessments

Ran VMware discovery from RVTools exports and an agentless collector, bridged an enterprise identity provider to IAM Identity Center, and modeled a Tanzu-to-EKS move with Karpenter. The compute savings are projections, not realized figures.

See the migration case studies

Incident root-cause analysis

Traced live failures to their low-level causes, from silent call-record ingestion loss to EKS ingress saturation, and wrote them up with the evidence and the fix.

Read an RCA write-up

Built end to end

Products I built and run myself

Two products I designed, built, secured, and operate alone, under a written working protocol for AI coding tools. They are not client deployments.

Document processing

PDF product, hardened and self-hosted

Took a serverless deployment that did not run to a self-audited WebAssembly engine, then moved it off Vercel to a self-hosted setup with verified payment handling.

First load 1.47 MB to 106 KB (~93%) · Nine security findings fixed

Read the hardening case study

Workforce

AI-assisted HR management tool

Leave, attendance, shifts, timesheets, and policy documents in one place. The assistant answers policy questions by quoting the source document and page.

Each company's data kept separate and tested · No outside AI service
